stimuli.text: The temperature of a liquid, in degrees Celsius, is modeled by a differentiable function $$H$$ of time $$t$$, in minutes. Selected values are shown.
The function $$f$$ is continuous on the closed interval $$[0, 4]$$. Selected values of $$f$$ are shown in the table.
The graph of the function $$f$$ shown consists of line segments on $$0 \leq x \leq 6$$.

image.alt: Graph of f: line segments through the points (0, 2), (1, -2), (2, -1), (3, -2), (4, -3), (5, 1), (6, 3).

stimuli.text: Let $$R$$ be the region enclosed by the graphs of $$f(x) = 4\cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)$$ and $$g(x) = x^2 - 2$$.

A particle moves in the xy-plane so that for $$0 \leq t \leq 3$$, $$\frac{dx}{dt} = 4\sin\left(\frac{t^2}{2}\right) + 1$$ and $$\frac{dy}{dt} = \cos(t)\,e^{t/4}$$. At $$t = 0$$ the particle is at $$(0, 3)$$.
People enter an amusement park at a rate modeled by a differentiable function $$P$$, where $$P(t)$$ is measured in people per minute and $$t$$ is measured in minutes. Selected values are shown.
The continuous function $$f$$ is defined on $$0 \leq x \leq 6$$. Its graph consists of line segments, as shown. Let $$g(x) = \int_{2}^{x} f(t)\,dt$$.

The function $$f$$ is defined by the power series $$f(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n+1}x^n}{n\cdot 5^n} = \frac{x}{5} - \frac{x^2}{2\cdot 25} + \frac{x^3}{3\cdot 125} - \cdots$$ for all $$x$$ in its interval of convergence.

questions.stem: What is the average rate of change of $$H$$ over the interval $$5 \leq t \leq 10$$, in degrees Celsius per minute?

options.why: This is the average temperature, not the average rate of change.
This is the total change in temperature; it still needs to be divided by the elapsed time.
This divides time by temperature, which is upside down.

questions.explanation: Average rate of change $$= \frac{H(10) - H(5)}{10 - 5} = \frac{33 - 56}{5} = -\frac{23}{5}$$ degrees per minute.

questions.stem: What is $$\int_{-1}^{0} \left(6x^{2} - 4x - 5\right)dx$$?

options.why: Correct. An antiderivative is $$F(x) = 2x^{3} - 2x^{2} - 5x$$; $$F(0) - F(-1) = -1$$.
This adds F(a) instead of subtracting it.
This is F(b) only; subtract F(a) as well.
This subtracts values of the integrand instead of an antiderivative.

questions.explanation: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, $$\int_{-1}^{0} f(x)\,dx = F(0) - F(-1)$$ with $$F(x) = 2x^{3} - 2x^{2} - 5x$$. That is $$0 - (1) = -1$$.

questions.stem: At what value of $$x$$ does the graph of $$f(x) = x^{3} + 9x^{2} - 3x + 4$$ have a point of inflection?

options.why: Sign error when solving f″(x) = 0.
This is −b/(2a), the vertex formula for a parabola, applied to the cubic's coefficients. Set f″(x) = 0 instead.
Inflection points are where f″ changes sign, not where f″ has its constant term.
Correct. $$f''(x) = 6x + 18$$ is zero and changes sign at $$x = -3$$.

questions.explanation: $$f'(x) = 3x^{2} + 18x - 3$$ and $$f''(x) = 6x + 18$$. $$f''$$ is linear, so it changes sign at its zero, $$x = -3$$.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = \begin{cases} -4x - 6 & x < -3 \\ 3x + 1 & x \geq -3 \end{cases}$$. What is $$\lim_{x \to -3^-} f(x)$$?

options.why: Correct. For $$x < -3$$, $$f(x) = -4x - 6$$, which approaches $$6$$.
One-sided limits can exist even when the two-sided limit does not.
This is the right-hand limit (and $$f(-3)$$). The left-hand limit uses the formula for $$x < -3$$.
This value doesn't come from substituting the approach point into the left-hand formula.

questions.explanation: The left-hand limit uses the piece for $$x < -3$$: $$-4(-3) - 6 = 6$$.

questions.stem: Let $$C(x)$$ be the cost, in dollars, of producing x items. Which of the following is the best interpretation of $$C'(3) = 6$$?

options.text: The cost when 3 items have been produced is 6.
options.why: This describes $$C(3)$$, the value of the function, not its rate of change.

options.text: The average rate of change of the cost over the first 3 items is 6 dollars per item.
options.why: The derivative is an instantaneous rate at one input, not an average over an interval.

options.text: The cost changes by 6 over the first 3 items.
options.why: This describes a total change over an interval, which is an integral of the rate, not the derivative at one point.

options.text: The cost is increasing at a rate of 6 dollars per item when 3 items have been produced.
options.why: Correct. A derivative at a point is an instantaneous rate of change, with units of output per unit of input.

questions.explanation: $$C'(3)$$ is the instantaneous rate of change of $$C$$ when 3 items have been produced. Its sign (positive) says the cost is increasing, and its units are dollars per item.

questions.stem: A particle moves in the plane with $$x'(t) = 8t$$ and $$y'(t) = 15t^2$$. What is the speed of the particle at $$t = 1$$?

options.why: This is the slope of the path, not the speed.
Speed is the magnitude of the velocity vector, not the sum of its components.
This forgets the square root.

questions.explanation: At $$t = 1$$, $$\vec{v} = \langle 8, 15 \rangle$$, so the speed is $$\sqrt{64 + 225} = 17$$.

options.why: This differentiates the outer power but leaves out the derivative of the inside function.
This applies the power rule to the derivative of the inside instead of to the inside function.
This is the value of the function, not its derivative.

questions.stem: A particle has velocity $$\vec{v}(t) = \langle 2t - 1, 3t^{2} - 2 \rangle$$ and position $$(-4, 5)$$ at $$t = 0$$. Where is the particle at $$t = 3$$?

options.why: Correct. Add the integral of each velocity component to the starting coordinate.
This is the displacement; add the starting position.
This is the velocity at the final time, not the position.
This adds the final velocity instead of the accumulated change in position.

questions.stem: Let $$y = f(x)$$ be the solution to $$\frac{dy}{dx} = x + y$$ with $$f(2) = 3$$. Using the tangent line at $$x = 2$$, what is the approximation of $$f(2.1)$$?

options.why: This adds the slope without multiplying by the step 0.1.
Sign error in the step.
This is only the estimated change; add it to f(a).

questions.explanation: At $$(2, 3)$$, $$\frac{dy}{dx} = 5$$. The tangent line gives $$f(2.1) \approx 3 + 5(0.1) = 3.5$$.

questions.stem: A function $$f$$ has $$f(3) = 1$$, $$f'(3) = -5$$, $$f''(3) = -6$$ and $$f'''(3) = -7$$. What is the coefficient of $$(x - 3)^3$$ in the Taylor polynomial for $$f$$ about $$x = 3$$?

options.why: This divides by 3 instead of $$3! = 6$$.
This is the coefficient of the squared term.
This forgets to divide by $$3!$$.

questions.explanation: The coefficient of $$(x - 3)^k$$ is $$\frac{f^{(k)}(3)}{k!}$$; for $$k = 3$$ it is $$\frac{-7}{6} = -\frac{7}{6}$$.

questions.stem: What is the least number of solutions that the equation $$f(x) = 0$$ must have on the interval $$[0, 4]$$?

options.why: This undercounts: each sign change between consecutive values guarantees its own zero.
Correct. The sign of $$f$$ changes 1 time between consecutive table values, and the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees a zero in each such interval.
The IVT only guarantees zeros where the sign changes; other zeros are possible but not required.
The IVT only guarantees zeros where the sign changes; other zeros are possible but not required.

questions.explanation: Because $$f$$ is continuous, the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees a solution of $$f(x) = 0$$ on every interval where the values change sign. Counting the sign changes in the table gives 1.

questions.stem: What is $$\int_1^{e} \ln x\,dx$$?

options.why: Sign error in the integration-by-parts formula.
This evaluates only part of the antiderivative or only one limit.
Correct. Integration by parts, then evaluate at both limits.
This drops the second term produced by integration by parts.

questions.explanation: Use integration by parts: $$\left[x\ln x - x\right]_1^{e} = (e - e) - (0 - 1) = 1$$.

questions.stem: The sum of $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n}$$ is approximated by its first 8 terms. What is the smallest upper bound on the error given by the alternating series error bound?

options.why: The exponent stays the same as in the series.
Correct. The error is at most the first omitted term.
This skips a term: the bound is the very next term.
This is the last term used, not the first one omitted.

questions.explanation: The terms alternate, decrease in size and approach 0, so $$|S - S_{8}| \leq b_{9} = \frac{1}{9}$$.

questions.stem: What is the coefficient of $$x^{4}$$ in the Maclaurin series for $$f(x) = e^{3x}$$?

options.why: The constant must be raised to the same power as x.
Correct. Substitute into the known Maclaurin series.
The denominator is $$n!$$, not $$n$$.
Sign error: check the sign pattern of the series.

questions.explanation: Replace $$x$$ by $$3x$$ in the series for $$e^x$$: the $$x^{4}$$ term is $$\frac{(3x)^{4}}{4!}$$, so the coefficient is $$\frac{27}{8}$$.

questions.stem: A particle moves along a line with velocity $$v(t) = t^{2} - t$$. What is the total distance traveled by the particle from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 2$$?

options.why: Correct. Total distance is $$\int_0^{2} |v(t)|\,dt$$; split at $$t = 1$$, where $$v$$ changes sign.
This is the velocity at the final time.
This counts the backward part twice.
This is the displacement; it subtracts the distance traveled backward.

questions.explanation: $$\int_0^{1} -v\,dt = \frac{1}{6}$$ and $$\int_{1}^{2} v\,dt = \frac{5}{6}$$. Total distance $$= 1$$.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n}{n^3}$$?

options.text: It converges, but to a negative sum only if the first term is negative.
options.why: This statement is not a classification of convergence.
Not this one: absolute values form a p-series with p = 3.
Correct. absolute values form a p-series with p = 3.
Not this one: absolute values form a p-series with p = 3.

questions.explanation: Test the absolute values first, then the series itself: absolute values form a p-series with p = 3.

questions.stem: Let $$y = f(x)$$ be the solution to $$\frac{dy}{dx} = x^2 - y$$ passing through the point $$(2, -1)$$. What is $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$$ at that point?

options.why: Sign error: the derivative of −y is −dy/dx.
This is dy/dx, the first derivative.
Correct. $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 2x - \frac{dy}{dx}$$, and $$\frac{dy}{dx} = 5$$ at the point.
This differentiates x² but treats y as a constant; y depends on x.

questions.explanation: Differentiate implicitly: $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 2x - \frac{dy}{dx} = 2x - (x^2 - y)$$. At $$(2, -1)$$: $$4 - 5 = -1$$.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = 2x^{3} - 9x^{2} + 12x$$. At what value of $$x$$ does $$f$$ have a relative minimum?

options.why: Correct. $$f'(x) = 6(x - 1)(x - 2)$$ changes from negative to positive at $$x = 2$$.
This is where f″ = 0 (the inflection point), not a critical point.
$$f(0) = 0$$, but $$f'(0)$$ is not zero, so this is not a critical point.
At this critical point $$f'$$ changes from positive to negative, which gives a relative maximum.

questions.explanation: $$f'(x) = 6x^2 - 18x + 12 = 6(x - 1)(x - 2)$$. Testing signs: $$f'$$ is positive left of $$1$$, negative between $$1$$ and $$2$$, positive right of $$2$$. So there is a relative maximum at $$1$$ and a relative minimum at $$2$$.

questions.stem: What is $$\int_0^{1} x\left(x^2 + 2\right)^{2}dx$$?

options.why: This forgets the factor $$\frac{1}{2}$$ from $$du = 2x\,dx$$.
After substituting, the limits must change to u-values (from c to 1 + c), not stay 0 to 1.
This evaluates only at the upper limit.
Correct. With $$u = x^2 + 2$$, $$du = 2x\,dx$$, the integral is $$\frac{1}{2}\int_{2}^{3} u^{2}\,du$$.

questions.stem: What is the radius of convergence of $$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{n\,(x + 1)^n}{5^n}$$?

options.why: The center is not the radius.
The radius is the reciprocal of this.
Correct. The ratio test gives $$\frac{|x + 1|}{5} < 1$$.
The series converges for all x only when the ratio limit is 0 for every x.

questions.explanation: $$\left|\frac{(n + 1)(x + 1)^{n+1}}{5^{n+1}}\cdot\frac{5^n}{n(x + 1)^n}\right| = \frac{n + 1}{n}\cdot\frac{|x + 1|}{5} \to \frac{|x + 1|}{5}$$. Convergence needs this below 1, so $$R = 5$$.

questions.stem: Which of the following gives the area of the region enclosed by the polar curve $$r = 3 + \sin\theta$$?

options.why: Correct. Polar area is half the integral of $$r^2$$ over one full trace.
The radius must be squared.
This leaves out the factor $$\frac{1}{2}$$.
Since $$r > 0$$ for every angle, the curve is traced once over $$[0, 2\pi]$$, not $$[0, \pi]$$.

questions.explanation: $$A = \frac{1}{2}\int_\alpha^\beta r^2\,d\theta$$. Because $$3 > 1$$, $$r > 0$$ for all $$\theta$$ and the curve closes after $$2\pi$$.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = \begin{cases} x^{2} - 3 & x \leq 2 \\ 2x - 3 & x > 2 \end{cases}$$. Which of the following is true?

options.why: The one-sided slopes differ, so $$f$$ is not differentiable.

options.text: $$f$$ is neither continuous nor differentiable at $$x = 2$$.
options.why: The one-sided limits match, so $$f$$ is continuous.

options.text: $$f$$ is continuous but not differentiable at $$x = 2$$.
options.why: Correct. The left piece gives $$f(2) = 1$$ with slope $$4$$; the right piece approaches $$1$$ with slope $$2$$. The values match but the slopes do not, so the graph has a corner.

options.text: $$f$$ is differentiable but not continuous at $$x = 2$$.
options.why: Differentiability implies continuity, so this can never happen.

questions.explanation: The left piece gives $$f(2) = 1$$ with slope $$4$$; the right piece approaches $$1$$ with slope $$2$$. The values agree (continuous), but the one-sided derivatives disagree (not differentiable).

questions.stem: If $$f(x) = \arctan(5x)$$, what is $$f'(2)$$?

options.why: The inside is squared as a whole: $$(5x)^2 = 25x^2$$.
This leaves out the inner derivative $$5$$.
This uses $$1 + x^2$$ in the denominator instead of $$1 + (5x)^2$$.
This leaves out the derivative of the upper limit, $$3x^{2}$$.
This evaluates the integrand at both limits; the derivative of an accumulation function only uses the variable limit.
The integrand must be evaluated at the upper limit, not at x.
Correct. By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus with the chain rule, substitute the upper limit and multiply by its derivative.

questions.stem: What is $$\int_0^{\infty} e^{-5x}\,dx$$?

options.why: Sign error: the integrand is positive, so the integral is positive.
The antiderivative of $$e^{-kx}$$ has a factor $$\frac{1}{k}$$, not $$k$$.
The exponential decays fast enough for the area to be finite.
Correct. $$\lim_{b \to \infty}\left[-\frac{1}{5}e^{-5x}\right]_0^b = \frac{1}{5}$$.

questions.explanation: $$\int_0^b e^{-5x}dx = \frac{1}{5}\left(1 - e^{-5b}\right) \to \frac{1}{5}$$.

questions.stem: A farmer has 72 meters of fencing to enclose a rectangular field along a straight river. No fence is needed along the river. What is the largest possible area of the field, in square meters?

options.why: This fences all four sides (a square), but the river side needs no fence.
This makes all three fenced sides equal, which is not optimal.
This doesn't account for the two equal sides perpendicular to the river.
Correct. With width $$x$$ perpendicular to the river, $$A = x(72 - 2x)$$, maximized at $$x = 18$$.

questions.explanation: $$A(x) = x(72 - 2x)$$, $$A'(x) = 72 - 4x = 0$$ at $$x = 18$$, and $$A'' = -4 < 0$$, so this is a maximum. The dimensions are $$18$$ by $$36$$, with area $$648$$.

questions.stem:
Which of the following series converge?

I. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n}{n}$$

II. $$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \left(\frac{5}{4}\right)^n$$

III. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^2 + 4}$$

options.why: Correct. I: converges (alternating series test, but the harmonic series diverges). II: diverges (geometric with |r| = 5/4 ≥ 1). III: converges (smaller than the convergent p-series with p = 2).
Check each series with an appropriate test: I converges, II diverges, III converges.
Check each series with an appropriate test: I converges, II diverges, III converges.
Check each series with an appropriate test: I converges, II diverges, III converges.

questions.explanation: Series I converges: alternating series test, but the harmonic series diverges. Series II diverges: geometric with |r| = 5/4 ≥ 1. Series III converges: smaller than the convergent p-series with p = 2.

questions.stem: A particle moves along a line with velocity $$v(t) = 3(t - 1)(t - 5)$$ for $$t \geq 0$$. For which values of $$t$$ is the particle speeding up?

options.why: This misses $$1 < t < 3$$, where both $$v$$ and $$a$$ are negative.
This is where the velocity is negative, which only means the particle moves left.
Correct. The particle speeds up when velocity and acceleration have the same sign.
On $$0 < t < 1$$ the velocity is positive but the acceleration is negative, so it is slowing down.

questions.explanation: $$a(t) = 6t - 18$$ changes sign at $$t = 3$$. $$v$$ is negative on $$(1, 5)$$ and positive elsewhere. Both are negative on $$(1, 3)$$ and both positive for $$t > 5$$.

questions.stem: What is the total area of the regions enclosed by the graphs of $$y = x^3$$ and $$y = x$$?

options.why: Correct. The graphs meet at $$x = -1, 0, 1$$. Each region has area $$\frac{1}{4}$$.
This integrates the difference across both regions at once; the signed areas cancel.
This is only one of the two regions.
This doubles the total area.

questions.explanation: On $$[-1, 0]$$, $$x^3$$ is on top; on $$[0, 1]$$, $$x$$ is on top. By symmetry, total area $$= 2\int_0^{1} (x - x^3)\,dx = 2 \cdot \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$$.

questions.stem: Let $$P_{2}(x)$$ be the degree-2 Taylor polynomial for $$f$$ about $$x = 0$$, and suppose $$|f^{(3)}(x)| \leq 12$$ for all $$x$$. What is the Lagrange error bound for $$|f(\frac{3}{4}) - P_{2}(\frac{3}{4})|$$?

options.why: This forgets to divide by $$(n + 1)!$$.
This uses the degree n instead of n + 1 for the factorial and power.
The distance from the center must be raised to the power n + 1.
Correct. $$\frac{12}{3!}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^{3}$$.

questions.stem: What is the sum of $$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} 6\left(-\frac{1}{5}\right)^n$$?

options.why: The formula is $$\frac{a}{1 - r}$$, not $$\frac{a}{1 + r}$$.
The first term depends on the starting index; check the term for the first value of n.
Correct. Geometric with first term $$6$$ and ratio $$-\frac{1}{5}$$.
This divides by $$r$$ instead of $$1 - r$$.

questions.explanation: $$|r| = \left|-\frac{1}{5}\right| < 1$$, so the series converges to $$\frac{6}{1 - \left(-\frac{1}{5}\right)} = 5$$.

questions.stem: What is the value of $$\int_{0}^{2} \ln(1 + x^2)\,dx$$?

options.why: Correct. Use the calculator's numerical integration.
This is a single rectangle using the right endpoint, a rough estimate rather than the integral.
This integrates over only half of the interval.
This is the change in the integrand, not the integral.

questions.explanation: On a graphing calculator, $$\int_{0}^{2} \ln(1 + x^2)\,dx \approx 1.433$$.

questions.stem: The temperature of a room, in degrees Fahrenheit, is modeled by $$H(t) = 81 + 9\sin\left(\frac{t}{8}\right)e^{-t/20}$$, where $$t$$ is measured in hours. What is the instantaneous rate of change of the temperature at $$t = 7$$, in degrees Fahrenheit per hour?

options.why: This is the average rate of change over $$0 \leq t \leq 7$$, not the instantaneous rate.
Correct. The calculator's numerical derivative of $$H$$ at $$t = 7$$ gives 0.265; the temperature is increasing.
This is the temperature itself, not its rate of change.
This multiplies the rate by the time, which is not a rate.

questions.explanation: The instantaneous rate of change is $$H'(7) \approx 0.265$$ degrees Fahrenheit per hour, from the calculator's numerical derivative.

questions.stem: A particle moves in the plane with $$x'(t) = 3\cos\left(\frac{t^2}{2}\right)$$ and $$y'(t) = e^{t/2}$$. What is the total distance the particle travels from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 3$$?

options.why: Correct. Integrate the speed $$\sqrt{x'(t)^2 + y'(t)^2}$$.
This adds the component displacements instead of integrating the speed.
This is the speed at the final time.
This is the straight-line distance between the start and end points.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the solution to $$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{x}{y}$$ with $$y(0) = 6$$?

options.why: The initial value is positive, so the positive root is needed.
This would have dy/dx = 1, which is not x/y.
Correct. $$y\,dy = x\,dx$$ gives $$y^2 = x^2 + C$$; $$C = 36$$, and the positive root matches $$y(0) = 6$$.
At $$x = 0$$ this gives $$\sqrt{6}$$, not $$6$$: the constant must be $$6^2$$.

questions.explanation: Separate: $$\int y\,dy = \int x\,dx$$, so $$\frac{y^2}{2} = \frac{x^2}{2} + C$$. With $$y(0) = 6$$, $$y^2 = x^2 + 36$$ and $$y = \sqrt{x^2 + 36}$$.

questions.stem: What is the coefficient of $$x^{4}$$ in the Maclaurin series for $$f(x) = \cos(3x)$$?

options.why: The denominator is $$n!$$, not $$n$$.
Sign error: check the sign pattern of the series.
Correct. Substitute into the known Maclaurin series.
The constant must be raised to the same power as x.

questions.explanation: Replace $$x$$ by $$3x$$ in the series for $$\cos x$$: the $$x^{4}$$ term is $$\frac{(3x)^{4}}{4!}$$, so the coefficient is $$\frac{27}{8}$$.

questions.stem: Sand is added to a pile at a rate modeled by $$R(t) = 14 + 4\sin\left(\frac{t}{9}\right)\sqrt{t + 1}$$ cubic feet per hour, for $$0 \leq t \leq 11$$. At time $$t = 0$$ the pile contains 213 cubic feet of sand. How much sand is in the pile at $$t = 11$$?

options.why: This adds the rate at one instant, not the accumulated amount.
This assumes the rate stays at R(T) for the whole time.
This is only the sand added; include the initial amount.

questions.explanation: Amount = initial amount + accumulated change = $$213 + \int_0^{11} R(t)\,dt \approx 213 + 220.578 = 433.578$$ cubic feet.

questions.stem:
Which of the following series converge?

I. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \cos\left(\frac{1}{n}\right)$$

II. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n!}{3^n}$$

III. $$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \left(\frac{5}{4}\right)^n$$

options.why: Check each series with an appropriate test: I diverges, II diverges, III diverges.
Check each series with an appropriate test: I diverges, II diverges, III diverges.
Check each series with an appropriate test: I diverges, II diverges, III diverges.
Correct. I: diverges (terms approach 1 (nth term test)). II: diverges (ratio test gives L = ∞). III: diverges (geometric with |r| = 5/4 ≥ 1).

questions.explanation: Series I diverges: terms approach 1 (nth term test). Series II diverges: ratio test gives L = ∞. Series III diverges: geometric with |r| = 5/4 ≥ 1.

questions.stem: What is the absolute maximum value of $$f(x) = xe^{-x/2} + \frac{\sin x}{4}$$ on the interval $$[0, 9]$$?

options.why: This evaluates f at the critical point of the first term alone; the sine term shifts the maximum.
This is the value at the right endpoint, which is not the largest.
Correct. Graph f on the calculator and find its maximum on the interval, checking the endpoints too.
This is where the maximum occurs (the x-value), not the maximum value.

questions.explanation: On the calculator, the maximum of $$f$$ on $$[0, 9]$$ occurs at $$x \approx 1.766$$, where $$f(x) \approx 0.976$$. The endpoint values are smaller.

questions.stem: What is the sum of $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} 7\left(-\frac{1}{6}\right)^n$$?

options.why: The formula is $$\frac{a}{1 - r}$$, not $$\frac{a}{1 + r}$$.
The first term depends on the starting index; check the term for the first value of n.
This divides by $$r$$ instead of $$1 - r$$.
Correct. Geometric with first term $$-\frac{7}{6}$$ and ratio $$-\frac{1}{6}$$.

questions.explanation: $$|r| = \left|-\frac{1}{6}\right| < 1$$, so the series converges to $$\frac{-\frac{7}{6}}{1 - \left(-\frac{1}{6}\right)} = -1$$.

questions.stem: What is the area of the region enclosed by the graphs of $$y = 2\cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)$$ and $$y = x^2 - 1$$?

options.why: Correct. The curves meet at $$x \approx -1.557$$ and $$x \approx 1.557$$; integrate top minus bottom.
This adds the absolute values of the curves instead of subtracting.
This is the distance between the intersection points, not an area.
This is the area under the top curve only.

questions.explanation: Store the intersection x-values from the calculator, then $$\int_{-1.557}^{1.557} \left(2\cos\frac{x}{2} - (x^2 - 1)\right)dx \approx 6.215$$.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = x^2 e^{-x}$$. What is the value of $$f'(2.5)$$?

options.why: This is the function value, not the derivative.
This is the derivative at $$x = 3.5$$, not at $$x = 2.5$$.
Correct. Use the calculator's numerical derivative (or the correct rule) at the given input.
This multiplies the derivatives of the factors instead of using the product rule.

questions.explanation: On a graphing calculator, evaluate $$\left.\frac{d}{dx}\left(x^2 e^{-x}\right)\right|_{x = 2.5} \approx -0.103$$.

questions.stem: What is the area of the region bounded by the polar curve $$r = 3 + 1.5\sin^2\theta + \frac{\cos 3\theta}{2}$$ and the rays $$\theta = 0$$ and $$\theta = \pi$$?

options.why: Correct. $$\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\pi} r^2\,d\theta$$ on the calculator.
The radius must be squared.
This leaves out the factor $$\frac{1}{2}$$.
